record.rationale: The exact submitted whole-case claim materially misstates the commanded calendar day and first/whole-order ending. I read the complete retained text at characters 0-850 and the cited operative span 390-849. The operative command requires flags on the White House and public buildings in the District of Columbia and State of Illinois to be at half mast on the day of the funeral service at Carrollton, Illinois, Wednesday, August 22, 1934. August 21, 1934 appears only in the signature block. The submitted first_end.date and whole_order_end.date are 1934-08-21, and the judgment_reason, research_rationale and source_notes repeatedly treat August 21 as the commanded day. Those exact conclusions contradict their own verified source. The whole-command calendar limitation supports expiration at the end of August 22, 1934 on the supplied text, without requiring proof of performance or funeral occurrence; it does not establish an August 21 ending. The source identifies EO:6826 through its closing number, Rainey subject and signature block. Its complete operative inventory contains one geographically bounded flag command, with no separate continuing command, savings clause or residual duty. Termination by the distant cutoff is consistent with that calendar limitation, but does not cure the erroneous exact lifecycle dates. No supplied source establishes an earlier ending, formal revocation, later amendment, revival, actual compliance or a current predicate requiring factual determination. I do not infer such events from absence. The claimed later-search coverage is qualified and does not independently prove the first ending. Rejection is scientific and rests on the source/date contradiction, not on the retained mechanical coverage limitations.
